q: An auditor uses a data analytics tool to compare 100% of a client's sales invoices to shipping records and identifies 14 invoices with no matching shipment. Which of the following is the auditor's most appropriate next step?
choices: Investigate the 14 exceptions to determine whether they represent misstatements or control deficiencies
Conclude that revenue is fairly stated because every item in the population was tested
Project the 14 exceptions to the population using a statistical sampling formula
Treat the exceptions as clearly trivial because they were identified by an automated tool
exp: Items flagged by an audit data analytic are exceptions that require follow-up to determine their nature and cause before the auditor can conclude. Projection is a sampling concept and is unnecessary when the full population was examined; the exceptions themselves are the known items to evaluate.

q: Before relying on a client-generated report of accounts receivable aging as input to an analytical procedure, the auditor should primarily obtain evidence about which of the following?
choices: Whether the report was prepared by someone independent of the credit function
The accuracy and completeness of the information in the report
Whether management has reviewed and signed the report
Whether the report format agrees with the prior-year report
exp: AU-C 500 requires the auditor to evaluate whether information produced by the entity is sufficiently reliable, including obtaining evidence about its accuracy and completeness. Management sign-off or consistent formatting does not establish that the underlying data is complete and accurate.

q: An auditor plans to rely on an automated three-way match control in the client's ERP system. The auditor tested the control in the prior year. Which of the following would best support a benchmarking strategy that reduces testing of the automated control this year?
choices: Management represents in writing that the control operated effectively all year
The control has been in place for more than three years
Effective IT general controls over program changes confirm the control has not been changed since it was last tested
The auditor tested a sample of manual journal entries and found no errors
exp: An automated control will continue to perform consistently unless the program is changed, so benchmarking depends on effective general IT controls (especially change management) showing the control is unchanged. A management representation is not sufficient evidence of operating effectiveness.

q: Which of the following is an example of a general IT control rather than an application control?
choices: An edit check rejecting a sales order with an invalid customer number
A batch total comparison of hours input to hours processed in payroll
An automated recalculation of invoice extensions
Restricting access to production programs to authorized IT personnel
exp: General IT controls apply to the IT environment broadly, such as access security, program change, and IT operations. Edit checks, batch totals, and automated calculations operate within a specific application over specific transactions and are application controls.

q: Under AU-C 315 (as clarified by SAS No. 145), how should an auditor approach the identification of general IT controls?
choices: Identify IT applications and aspects of the IT environment subject to risks arising from IT, then identify general IT controls that address those risks
Test all general IT controls in every audit regardless of planned reliance on controls
Identify general IT controls only when the client uses a service organization
Identify general IT controls only for public entities subject to PCAOB standards
exp: SAS 145 requires the auditor to identify the IT applications and other aspects of the IT environment that are subject to risks arising from the use of IT, and then the related general IT controls that address those risks. It does not require testing all general IT controls in every audit.

q: An auditor uses an audit data analytic to recalculate depreciation for every fixed asset in the population and finds no differences above a small threshold. The analytic is best characterized as which type of procedure?
choices: A risk assessment procedure only
A substantive procedure that may provide evidence about valuation of depreciation expense
A test of controls over the fixed asset subledger
A walkthrough of the fixed asset process
exp: Recalculation of depreciation for the population is a substantive test of details that provides direct evidence about the amounts recorded. It does not test whether a control operated, and it goes beyond risk assessment because it is designed to detect material misstatement.

q: A client outsources payroll processing to a service organization. The user auditor intends to rely on controls at the service organization. Which report would most directly support that reliance?
choices: A SOC 1 Type 1 report describing the design of controls at a point in time
A SOC 3 report intended for general use
A SOC 1 Type 2 report on the description, design, and operating effectiveness of controls over a period
A SOC 2 Type 2 report on security and availability controls
exp: Under AU-C 402, reliance on operating effectiveness requires evidence over a period, which a Type 2 report on controls relevant to financial reporting (SOC 1) provides. A Type 1 report addresses design and implementation only, and SOC 2/SOC 3 address trust services criteria rather than internal control over financial reporting.

q: A SOC 1 Type 2 report states that the service organization's controls are effective only if user entities implement certain complementary user entity controls. What should the user auditor do?
choices: Ignore the complementary controls because the service auditor already tested them
Request that the service auditor extend testing to the user entity
Modify the opinion for a scope limitation
Evaluate whether the user entity has designed and implemented the complementary user entity controls and, if relying on them, test them
exp: Complementary user entity controls are the user entity's responsibility, so the user auditor must consider them at the user entity (AU-C 402). The service auditor does not test controls at user entities, which is the trap in assuming they are already covered.

q: An auditor uses software to stratify the accounts payable population and select all vendors with balances above a threshold plus a sample of the remainder. The software is most appropriately described as being used to:
choices: Select items for testing
Evaluate the operating effectiveness of IT general controls
Replace the need for confirmation or other substantive procedures
Assess control risk at the maximum
exp: Stratification and selection of key items is a selection technique; the selected items still must be tested with substantive procedures. Using software to select items does not itself provide evidence about controls or eliminate further testing.

q: When an auditor's data analytic is applied to the full population of journal entries and produces a large number of items meeting the criteria, which of the following responses is most appropriate?
choices: Select a haphazard sample of the flagged items and conclude on the rest without further consideration
Refine the criteria or further disaggregate the results to identify the items that represent a higher risk of misstatement and investigate those
Discard the analytic and revert to traditional sampling
Report all flagged items to those charged with governance as significant deficiencies
exp: When an analytic produces many 'false positives,' the auditor typically refines the expectation or criteria to isolate notable items that warrant investigation. Flagged items are not automatically control deficiencies, and abandoning the analytic ignores useful evidence.

q: Which of the following best describes the purpose of an integrated test facility (ITF)?
choices: To extract data from client files for analysis on the auditor's computer
To compare two versions of a program to detect unauthorized changes
To process fictitious auditor transactions through the client's live system alongside actual transactions and compare results to expectations
To monitor online transactions continuously by embedding audit modules
exp: An ITF creates a dummy entity in the live system so auditor test data is processed with real data, testing processing controls. Generalized audit software extracts and analyzes data, and parallel simulation or code comparison addresses different objectives.

q: An auditor reprocesses actual client payroll data using the auditor's own program and compares the output to the client's payroll register. This technique is:
choices: Test data
Integrated test facility
Embedded audit module
Parallel simulation
exp: Parallel simulation uses the auditor's software to reprocess real client data and compare results. Test data and ITF instead run auditor-created transactions through the client's programs.

q: Which risk arising from IT is most directly addressed by effective segregation between program development and production environments?
choices: Unauthorized changes to programs that process financial data
Data loss from inadequate backup procedures
Inaccurate data entry by end users
Failure of the client to respond timely to customer inquiries
exp: Separating development from production, with controlled migration, addresses the risk that unauthorized or untested program changes reach the systems that process transactions. Backup and data entry risks are addressed by other controls.

q: An entity's sales application allows a sales manager to both create new customers and override credit limits. Which IT-related deficiency does this most directly represent?
choices: Inadequate backup and recovery
Inadequate logical access controls that fail to enforce segregation of duties
An ineffective program change process
A data conversion error
exp: Access rights that let one user perform incompatible functions reflect a logical access/segregation of duties deficiency. Program change and backup controls address different risks.

q: An auditor uses an audit data analytic during planning to compare monthly gross margin by product line to prior years and industry data. The primary purpose of this analytic is to:
choices: Provide sufficient appropriate evidence to support the opinion on revenue
Test the operating effectiveness of revenue controls
Identify unusual relationships that may indicate risks of material misstatement
Satisfy the requirement for an overall review near the end of the audit
exp: Analytical procedures used as risk assessment procedures (AU-C 315, AU-C 520) help identify unusual relationships that may indicate risks. A planning analytic alone is generally not designed to provide substantive evidence sufficient to support conclusions.

q: When using an analytic as a substantive analytical procedure under AU-C 520, which of the following is required?
choices: The auditor must test 100% of the population
The expectation must be developed by the client's management
The difference must be investigated only if it exceeds overall materiality
The auditor must develop an expectation precise enough to identify a misstatement that could be material and determine the acceptable difference
exp: AU-C 520 requires the auditor to develop a sufficiently precise expectation from reliable data and determine the amount of difference that is acceptable without further investigation. The threshold is usually set below overall materiality, and the expectation should be the auditor's, not management's.

q: An auditor uses an AI-enabled tool provided by the firm to analyze lease contracts. Under the firm's quality management system, which statement is most accurate?
choices: The engagement team remains responsible for determining that the tool is appropriate for the engagement and for evaluating its output
Because the firm approved the tool, the engagement team may accept its output without evaluation
Using the tool shifts responsibility for the conclusions to the tool vendor
Output of firm-approved tools need not be documented
exp: Under SQMS 1 and the engagement-level standards, firm-approved technological resources still require the engagement team to use them appropriately and exercise professional judgment over their output. Firm approval does not remove the team's responsibility or documentation requirements.

q: An auditor identified that the client's password parameters were weak but tested and found effective compensating controls over user access reviews. The auditor's most appropriate conclusion regarding automated application controls that depend on access security is:
choices: Automated controls cannot be relied upon under any circumstances
Reliance on the automated controls may still be appropriate if the compensating controls address the risk
The auditor must issue an adverse opinion on the financial statements
The auditor must perform a 100% test of all transactions
exp: A general IT control deficiency requires the auditor to evaluate its effect, and effective compensating controls can mitigate the risk so reliance on dependent application controls may remain appropriate. An IT deficiency does not automatically preclude reliance or affect the opinion on the financial statements.

q: An auditor extracts the client's entire general ledger and uses software to identify journal entries posted on weekends, by unusual users, or with round-dollar amounts. These procedures most directly respond to which requirement?
choices: Obtaining an understanding of the entity's industry
Evaluating going concern
Testing the appropriateness of journal entries to address the risk of management override of controls
Confirming balances with third parties
exp: AU-C 240 requires procedures to test journal entries and other adjustments for management override; analytics that identify entries with fraud-risk characteristics are a common approach. The other procedures address different audit objectives.

q: Which of the following attributes of data is most important when an auditor evaluates the reliability of external data (for example, an industry price index) used in an analytic?
choices: Whether the data is presented in the same format as the client's records
Whether the data was purchased rather than obtained free
Whether management prefers the source
The source's competence and objectivity, and whether the data is relevant to the assertion
exp: Under AU-C 500 (as amended by SAS 142), the auditor considers the relevance and reliability of information, including the source's competence, objectivity, and any bias. Format, cost, or management preference do not determine reliability.

q: An auditor's analytic compares the dates of shipment on the shipping log to invoice dates for all sales near year-end. This analytic primarily provides evidence about which assertion?
choices: Cutoff
Presentation
Rights and obligations
Valuation
exp: Comparing shipment dates to invoice dates around period-end tests whether sales are recorded in the proper period, which is the cutoff assertion. It does not address valuation of receivables or ownership.

q: The use of cloud computing by a client most directly affects the auditor's understanding of which of the following?
choices: The applicable financial reporting framework
The entity's IT environment, including reliance on third-party providers and related controls
The determination of overall materiality
The auditor's independence
exp: Cloud hosting means a third party performs IT functions, so the auditor considers the IT environment, risks arising from IT, and whether service organization reporting (for example, a SOC 1) is needed. Cloud use does not change the reporting framework or materiality.

q: For which of the following would a test of an automated control typically require the smallest sample, assuming effective general IT controls?
choices: A manual control performed daily
A manual control performed weekly
An automated control, which can often be tested with one or a few instances
A manual review control performed quarterly
exp: Because automated controls perform consistently when general IT controls are effective, a test of one or a few instances can suffice. Manual controls are subject to human error, so sample sizes depend on frequency and are larger.

q: An auditor wants evidence that all approved credit memos were recorded. Using a data analytic, the auditor should compare:
choices: Recorded credit memos in the sales returns journal to the approved credit memo file
Customer remittances to the cash receipts journal
Recorded credit memos to the shipping log
The approved credit memo file to recorded credit memos in the sales returns journal
exp: Completeness is tested by tracing from source documents (approved credit memos) to the accounting records. Tracing from the journal back to documents tests occurrence, which is the reversed-direction trap.

q: In an integrated audit under PCAOB AS 2201, the auditor's evaluation of IT includes which of the following?
choices: Understanding how IT affects the flow of transactions and identifying risks arising from IT that relate to relevant assertions
Testing every IT general control at the entity regardless of relevance to financial reporting
Issuing a separate opinion on the effectiveness of the entity's IT security
Relying on the client's IT department testing without evaluation
exp: AS 2201 requires the auditor to understand IT's effect on the flow of transactions and to address risks arising from IT that are relevant to ICFR. It does not require testing irrelevant IT controls or a separate IT security opinion.

q: A client converted to a new general ledger system mid-year. Which procedure most directly addresses the risk of misstatement from the conversion?
choices: Inquire of IT about user satisfaction with the new system
Test controls over data conversion, such as reconciliations of balances transferred from the old system to the new system
Review the vendor's marketing material about the system
Increase overall materiality because the new system is more reliable
exp: Data conversion creates a risk that balances are incompletely or inaccurately transferred, so the auditor tests conversion controls or reconciles balances. User satisfaction and vendor claims provide no evidence about transferred data.

q: An auditor identifies a significant risk of revenue recognition and plans to address it only with a substantive analytical procedure using disaggregated data. Under AU-C 330, which is correct?
choices: This is acceptable because analytics provide stronger evidence than tests of details
This is never acceptable for revenue
When the approach to a significant risk consists only of substantive procedures, those procedures must include tests of details
This is acceptable only if the auditor also obtains a management representation
exp: AU-C 330 requires that if the response to a significant risk consists only of substantive procedures, it must include tests of details. Analytics alone are insufficient in that case; a representation letter does not substitute.

q: Which of the following is the best example of evidence that the auditor has addressed the reliability of data used in an audit data analytic?
choices: The analytic produced results consistent with the auditor's expectation
The client's IT manager confirmed the data was extracted correctly
The data was provided in a spreadsheet
The auditor reconciled the extracted data's record counts and totals to the general ledger and tested relevant controls over the data
exp: Reconciling extracted data to the ledger and testing controls over its generation provide evidence of completeness and accuracy (AU-C 500). Results matching expectations can be circular if the data itself is unreliable, and a verbal confirmation is weak evidence.

q: A small client uses off-the-shelf accounting software that does not allow source code modification. How does this most likely affect the auditor's consideration of general IT controls over program changes?
choices: Risks from program changes are likely lower, so fewer program change controls may be relevant
Program change controls must be tested more extensively
The auditor must obtain a SOC 1 Type 2 report from the software vendor
The auditor cannot rely on any automated calculations
exp: When software cannot be modified, the risk of unauthorized program changes is reduced, so the auditor scales the understanding of related general IT controls. Packaged software does not automatically require a vendor SOC 1 report or preclude reliance on automated functionality.

q: An auditor's analytic identifies a vendor whose bank account matches an employee's direct deposit account. This finding most likely indicates a heightened risk of:
choices: Lapping of customer receipts
Fictitious vendor or disbursement fraud
Improper revenue cutoff
Understated inventory
exp: A vendor bank account matching an employee's account is a classic indicator of a fictitious vendor scheme to divert disbursements. Lapping involves customer cash receipts, not vendor payments.
